body:
After #2682 reuses tokenized prefixes across requests, the frontend still rebuilds the prompt's block-hash chain on each turn. This change lets the same cached prefix retain immutable prompt block hashes and extend them from the tokenizer's exact matched boundary, reducing repeated host work for growing conversations.

- Keep token IDs and their prompt block hashes under the same `ATOM_TOKENIZE_CACHE_MB` byte budget, with no retained parent-record chain. Reuse complete blocks only; recompute a partial boundary block together with the appended tokens.
- Reuse the cached block hashes when building the existing frontend prompt-hash chain (request fanout shares one chain). They stay on the frontend: only the chain rides the ADD frame, as before. It is used when its block size, seed, token count and block count fit, with ordinary hashing as the fallback; the prompt is fingerprinted once per request, and the engine checks the shipped chain (fingerprint and sampled links) as before. BlockManager still determines actual KV residency, so a tokenizer hit cannot become a false KV hit after eviction.
- Only the prompt block-hash chain is kept (content hashes; KV residency stays with BlockManager). This PR adds no PAGE/STATE storage adapter, metadata cache, lookup cancellation or DualPath routing.

Enabled by default when prefix caching, frontend prefix hashing and a compatible tokenizer cache are active. Set `ATOM_TOKENIZE_CACHE_BLOCK_HASHES=0` to disable shared prompt block hashes. Short prompts, unsupported tokenizers, token-ID inputs and multimodal inputs retain the existing path. The benchmark-only catalog override is excluded from this PR.

### Validation

- Targeted Linux CPU suite at the benchmark revision: **156 passed** (latest revision) across `test_segment_tokenizer.py`, `test_prefix_block_hashes.py`, `test_io_processor_fanout.py` and `test_admission_host_overhead.py`. Coverage includes prompt rewrites/forks, wrapper and partial-block boundaries, seed/geometry changes, byte-budget eviction, concurrent requests, disable/fallback behavior, fanout/IPC and actual HBM eviction.
- The implementation retains no per-request timer or reuse-counter fields. Tests observe actual hash calls to check incremental reuse. After this cleanup, 14 unified-prefix leaf cases and 39 existing segment-tokenizer tests pass locally. These local tests load the actual leaf modules while bypassing the Linux-only package initializer on Windows; they do not cover frontend/IPC integration, which remains with Linux PR CI. Black, Ruff and `git diff --check` pass for the changed files.
- Default-on, explicit enable (`1`) and explicit disable (`0`) flag parsing checks pass. The existing processor-initialization test now leaves the flag unset to exercise the default path.
- Full repository CI is left to the PR checks; the targeted suite above is not a claim that the entire test suite has passed.

### 🏷️ CI Guide

**Runs automatically on every eligible PR before approval:**
- ✅ Pre Checkin: Black, Ruff, catalog schema validation, non-GPU unit tests

**Heavy model tests:**
- ✅ Run after the PR is approved and Pre Checkin passes
- ✅ Run immediately when an approval review is submitted
- ✅ Can be requested before approval with labels

| Label | Tests |
|-------|-------|
| `ci:full` | Run all heavy PR model tests: native ATOM, vLLM, and SGLang |
| `ci:atom` | Run native ATOM model accuracy tests |
| `ci:vllm` | Run ATOM vLLM OOT model accuracy tests |
| `ci:sglang` | Run ATOM SGLang model accuracy tests |

> Heavy jobs are skipped when the PR is not approved and no matching `ci:*` label is present.
> Add labels via the sidebar or `gh pr edit 2716 --add-label <label>`

2 previously missed issues In code that hasn't changed since last review
Avoid serializing the hash chain twice in ADD frames `atom/​model_engine/​prefix_hash.py:107` [verified] When a projection is attached, the ADD frame serializes the complete hash chain twice: in `hashes` and in `projection.kv_hashes`. BlockManager adopts only `hashes`, while `prompt_prefix` keeps the redundant projection alive, adding serialization work and retained memory on the default path. Use one packed representation for both records, or keep the projection frontend-only and update the IPC tests accordingly.
Avoid prefix projection work when prefix caching is disabled `atom/​model_engine/​segment_tokenizer.py:280` [verified] Tokenizers with overlapping added tokens can support segment caching while setting `_prefix_ok = False`, so `_find_prefix` always misses and `_store_prefix` retains no projection. This branch still builds a full projection on every eligible request, adding fingerprinting and copying without any cross-request hash reuse. Require `_prefix_ok` here so these tokenizers retain the ordinary frontend hashing path.

### 🔵 Needs a closer look Duplicate IPC hash payloads and projection creation without reuse opportunities add avoidable recurring host overhead. **No open issues** 🎉
2 previously missed issues In code that hasn't changed since last review
Avoid duplicating block hashes in ADD request projections `atom/​model_engine/​prefix_hash.py:107` Including the projection serializes every block hash twice in each successful ADD request: once in `hashes` and again in `projection.kv_hashes`. The engine consumes `hashes` but retains the redundant bytes through `seq.prompt_prefix`, which has no production reader. Keep the projection frontend-only, or use a single hash payload for transport and reconstruct any needed projection metadata on receipt.
Skip uncached projections when no prefix cut is eligible `atom/​model_engine/​segment_tokenizer.py:284` With `_prefix_ok=True`, a long prompt with no added-token cuts beyond `_PREFIX_KEY_CHARS` cannot store a prefix, yet this builds a full projection on every request. When there is also no cached projection to reuse, the extra fingerprinting and copying provide no cross-request hash savings. Use ordinary frontend hashing unless a cached projection is available or a new cut is eligible for prefix storage.
